newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to evacuate 5,000 from Iraqi Kurdistan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to evacuate 5,000 from Iraqi Kurdistan.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it was planning to evacuate about 5,000 people, including employees of non-governmental organisations and their families, from Kurdish areas of northern Iraq.

State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said the workers and their families, including some who were not ethnic Kurds, would be flown to the Pacific Ocean island of Guam in the second such airlift from the area, which has been harrassed by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.

Davies said: "We intend to move forward with the departure from Northern Iraq of local employees of U.S.-funded and/or U.S.-based NGOs and their family members." He said this involved employees of 24 different organizations.

Discussions were under way on the practicalities of the evacuation with Turkey, a NATO ally which shares a border with Iraq, and it was hoped the flights would begin in a few weeks. He said there was a continuing risk for these people and the government had decided "since we can do it we should do it."

Many NGO workers, who had supported relief efforts in the mountainous region, fled their towns when Saddam's troops entered the Western-protected area at the invitation of one of two rival Kurdish factions, the Kurdish Democratic Party.

In September about 2,000 former employees of U.S. government agencies in Kurdistan were evacuated. They were flown from the eastern Turkish city of Diyarbakir to Guam, where they were processed for asylum in the United States.
